transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood SE), Liam Carter (Redwood Partner Ops), Jordan Patel (Crestline Head of Partnerships), Sofia Martinez (Crestline BDR), Rajesh Iyer (Crestline CTO), Hannah Lee (Crestline Procurement)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect):
Redwood and Crestline reviewed the co-sell pipeline, prioritized three target deals (one in pilot, two in opportunity stage), discussed technical validation needs (latency/cost benchmarks, SOC2/KMS questions), and agreed on next steps: share joint pipeline spreadsheet, run a short benchmark for the pilot, and schedule an exec intro. Procurement flagged standard timeline and asked for security docs and SSO/KMS info.

Topics:
- Current pipeline and top deals
- Pilot scope and technical success criteria
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, VPC)
- Commercial split and co-sell motions
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call then we'll jump into the pipeline. I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on the partner motion.
[00:12] Jordan Patel: Jordan here, Crestline - thanks, Maya.
[00:14] Sofia Martinez: Sofia - joining from Partnerships ops.
[00:17] Ethan Ruiz: Ethan here, SE.
[00:19] Rajesh Iyer: Rajesh, CTO.
[00:21] Hannah Lee: Hannah from procurement.
[00:24] Liam Carter: Liam, Partner Ops Redwood. Nice to meet you all.

[00:30] Maya Chen: Cool. Quick agenda we asked Jordan to share the joint pipeline, we'll go top-down on three priority deals, then technical ask for the pilot and procurement questions, and wrap with next steps. Jordan, you wanna kick off with the pipeline?
[00:40] Jordan Patel: Yeah, sure. So the big ones for us right now Deal A is a pilot with a fintech customer, they want a hosted API initially; Deal B is an enterprise retail chain looking for VPC/private deployment; Deal C is a healthcare customer exploring a POC. I sent a sheet earlier, it's in the deck link but quick tl;dr - A is hot (legal + security smoke tests pending), B is earlier but high ACV, C has regulatory constraints.
[01:10] Maya Chen: Great. For A, when you say hosted API, does Crestline intend to introduce Redwood's hosted offering to the end customer, or are they expecting Crestline to host on their AWS account?
[01:22] Jordan Patel: Good question. For A they want hosted initially speed to value. For B they're asking for private/VPC, likely dedicated or private deployment. C is murky could be private on-prem.
[01:34] Ethan Ruiz: From a SE perspective, for Deal A if they're ok with hosted we can run a lightweight benchmark on our hosted endpoint. We'll want sample prompts and expected latency SLOs and token volume.
[01:45] Rajesh Iyer: For the pilot, we really need the SLO targets 100-200ms per token isn't realistic for longer generation but overall latency per request <800ms is what they told us. Also cost per 1k tokens is important for their procurement.
[01:58] Sofia Martinez: And we should note the champion at fintech is product lead Emma Rhodes, she's pretty technical and will ask about KV cache and warm start behavior.
[02:10] Maya Chen: Good to know. We'll include KV cache behavior in the benchmark notes. Quick note sometimes our automatic transcript shows K V cache or KV cash, so ignore that.
[02:19] Jordan Patel: ha, yeah transcription typo noted.

[02:25] Ethan Ruiz: For the benchmark I'll ask for sample prompt set, expected concurrency, and sequence lengths. If you can share a sample set we can run on our infra and give a numbers doc back in about a week. That should cover latency and token cost estimates.
[02:41] Rajesh Iyer: Are you able to run on quantized model variants? For our costs they'd like to see 8-bit or q4 style runs.
[02:49] Ethan Ruiz: We can run on multiple model variants we'll note tradeoffs. If the pilot wants fastest time to market, hosted on a balanced quantization profile usually hits good cost/latency. For private/Dedicated we can surface quantization and kernel choices but that requires more ops work.

[03:05] Hannah Lee: From procurement, timeline worst case legal and security review will be 3 to 4 weeks after we get SOC2 and security docs. Can you send SOC2 report and details about KMS/HSM? Also SSO we use SAML, need SAML SSO integration details.
[03:20] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll send SOC2, our security whitepaper, and a short note on SSO/SAML and KMS integration. We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and envelope encryption for hosted.
[03:33] Jordan Patel: For B (retail) they will require audit logs and longer data retention controls. Is that in your Private offering?
[03:41] Liam Carter: Yes, Private supports detailed audit logs and retention configs. We can also ship additional retention settings under an enterprise add-on. We'll note that in the doc.

[03:50] Sofia Martinez: On go-to-market are we planning a joint AH (account health) meeting for each deal? What's the standard co-sell split?
[03:59] Maya Chen: Typically for co-sell we coordinate motion: Crestline handles intro and first touch, Redwood supports technical validation and commercial terms. Revenue split varies case-by-case we'll propose a standard partner discount matrix in the joint pipeline sheet.
[04:13] Jordan Patel: Can you include estimated ACV ranges and suggested partner discount tiers? That helps our reps know what to position.
[04:20] Maya Chen: Will do. We'll add suggested tiers (pilot, expansion, enterprise) + recommended discount ranges and who owns renewal.

[04:30] Rajesh Iyer: Technical deep dive question for the private deployment, what's your recommended network topology? We need to keep traffic egress minimal, and also ensure log forwarding to our SIEM.
[04:41] Ethan Ruiz: For VPC private we recommend a restricted egress NAT for outgoing model fetches only, plus VPC peering or PrivateLink for data plane. Log forwarding can be configured to push to your SIEM via syslog or secure S3 bucket with lifecycle. We'll draft topology diagrams.
[04:58] Rajesh Iyer: Good, please include sample IaC snippets if possible.
[05:03] Ethan Ruiz: Yep, we'll include Terraform blocks and an example CloudFormation snippet.

[05:10] Hannah Lee: On procurement paperwork do you need our vendor questionnaire completed, or do you provide a standard attestation?
[05:18] Maya Chen: We normally complete vendor questionnaires for enterprise deals. For partners we can also provide standard templates back. If you send the form, we'll have legal answer within their timeline.

[05:28] Jordan Patel: Quick ask for Deal A champion Emma wants a short sandbox with redwood that they can test with internal data, but they can't send PII. Is there an easy way to isolate test data and have TTL?
[05:40] Ethan Ruiz: You can spin up a hosted sandbox with data masking and short retention, or do a private demo in a test VPC. For hosted sandbox we can set 7-day retention and disable full logs for that instance. We'll document the options.

[05:55] Maya Chen: Alright, wrapping up recap of next steps: Maya to share joint pipeline spreadsheet and partner discount tiers; Ethan to run the benchmark for Deal A and share numbers; Jordan to coordinate exec intro; Hannah to confirm procurement timeline and send vendor questionnaire. Anything else?
[06:10] Sofia Martinez: Can we get an introductory slide for reps that summarizes the co-sell motion? Something we can include in Crestline sales enablement.
[06:18] Liam Carter: Yes we'll add a 1-pager partner playbook with talk tracks and escalation.

[06:25] Jordan Patel: One more thing competitors: the fintech looked at Anthropic and AWS Bedrock too. They asked about model comparatives. Can Redwood provide a brief competitive one-pager?
[06:35] Maya Chen: We'll include a short competitive comparison and performance notes. Note that some model names might be mis-transcribed in these notes.

[06:42] Rajesh Iyer: Any blockers from your side on data residency? The healthcare prospect for Deal C is strict about EU residency.
[06:49] Maya Chen: For Private we can deploy in EU regions or on-prem. We'll include residency options and the associated timelines.

[06:58] Hannah Lee: Procurement will likely need a point of contact for any security clarifications who's our go-to?
[07:04] Maya Chen: I'll be the primary contact for commercial and partner ops, Ethan will handle technical security questions, and Liam will own partner ops. I'll put our contact info in the pipeline sheet.

[07:15] Jordan Patel: Great. Thanks everyone this feels actionable.
[07:19] Maya Chen: Thanks we'll send the docs and proposed dates.
[07:22] Sofia Martinez: Thanks all.
[07:24] (meeting ends)
